newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine bans prominent analytical TV programme.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine bans prominent analytical TV programme.

text.p: Ukrainian broadcasting authorities axed a flagship analytical television programme on Friday in a move which its editor blamed on pressure from leftist politicians irritated by an item on Cuba.

The National Council for Television and Radio said in a letter that Pislyamova (Postscript), which had a prime-time slot on Sundays, was being taken off the air as it did not match the company's programming concept.

The letter, faxed to Reuters by Studio One Plus One which makes Pislyamova, also demanded copies of last week's edition which included an item on Cuba from a visit there by parliamentary speaker and Socialist Party head Olexander Moroz.

"This is typical political censorship by the National Council under pressure from leftist Ukrainian forces who think freedom of speech in Ukraine is the same thing as in Cuba," said Olexander Tkachenko, One Plus One's news editor.

The council could not immediately be contacted for comment. Its decision followed a verbal complaint by the Cuban embassy to the Foreign Ministry about the programme, which included coverage of unemployment on Cuba and of women working as prostitutes.
Cuba's acting ambassador accused the programme of bias and asked the council to take steps against One Plus One.
"The commentary included open insults to the Cuban people, in particular Cuban women, and its leader," he wrote in a letter to the council.
